main_body: Flat grass ground patch with repeating 16px tufts, 4x3 tiles. It is a terrain tile, not a standing object.
top_band: none; ground texture with no top/front structure
evidence: Terrain kind: a flat ground patch of grass. The column scan shows a repeating 16-row tuft pattern, not a standing object, so the 3/4 contract (top band + front face) does not apply. No side faces or standing volume are drawn. Nothing in Part A is violated for ground.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 6 distinct colours and a median of 6 per tile, against 80 distinct colours and 26 per tile in the grass reference. Its shading is limited to about 4 greens (dark, mid, light, highlight) and the tufts are one identical 16px motif repeated across the patch, so the tiling is plain and obvious. The orange pixels at regular intervals look like marker dots rather than grass detail. Dark pixels are green-tinted (0% neutral), which is acceptable, and flat-fill coverage is 0%. Even so, it is far below the grass reference in colour variety, tuft variety and tile density, so it looks thinner and more mechanical next to it.
